newsitem.title: JAPAN: Iridium prices surge on demand for new engine.
newsitem.headline: Iridium prices surge on demand for new engine.

text.p: Iridium prices have surged, especially in the past month, backed by strong physical demand related to a new engine which Mitsubishi Motors Corp introduced in Japan last summer, Japanese traders said on Tuesday.
They said the autocatalyst in the engine uses iridium, although Mitsubishi Motors declined to comment on which metals are used in the engine.

The gasoline-direct-injection (GDI) engine, is fitted in the Galant, a medium-sized sedan, and the Legnum station wagon. The company says the engine is 10 percent more powerful, 35 percent more fuel-efficient and cuts carbon dioxide emissions by 35 percent compared with conventional engines.
Spot iridum was quoted at around $125.00 per ounce as of Tuesday, sharply up from around $80 in mid-December and around $50 at the end of May last year.
Iridium production is typcally a by-product in platinum mining.

"Large-lot physical buying, perhaps around one tonne of iridium, has been detected. The buying was believed to be for Mitsubishi Motors' autocatalyst. As a result, the spot market is currently extremely tight," one trading house trader said.
South Africa accounts for nearly 100 percent of global iridium output, with annual global production estimated at around four tonnes.
Traders said iridium prices are likely to rise further amid limited global production.
"The bullish trends are likely to continue at least for the rest of the year. Iridium could rise to around $250 per ounce during this year amid limited production capacity," another trader said.
